title: Athens and Sparta

cards.h: Two cities, two crazy ways to live
cards.b:
Athens gave us democracy, theatre and philosophy. Sparta gave us a state where boys were taken from their mothers at seven to become soldiers.

They fought together against Persia. Then they fought each other for 27 years.

In 508/507 BCE, a reformer called Cleisthenes reorganised Athens so ordinary citizens shared power. The Assembly met on a hill, the Pnyx. Any male citizen could speak and vote. Many officials were picked by lottery.

Citizens could also vote to exile a leader for ten years. This was ostracism, named after the pottery shards used as ballots.
Only adult male citizens voted. Women, slaves and foreigners did not. Perhaps 30,000-40,000 men could vote in a population of several hundred thousand. Athens was a democracy for a minority.

Spartan boys entered the agoge at about seven. They trained, went hungry and learned to endure. Adults were full-time soldiers.

Who grew the food? The helots, enslaved Greeks the Spartans ruled by terror. Spartans lived in constant fear of a helot revolt. Spartan women had more freedom than Athenian women, including owning land.

In 480 BCE King Leonidas of Sparta held the narrow pass at Thermopylae against Xerxes's huge army and died with his men. After Persia's defeat, Athens grew rich and built the Parthenon (447-432 BCE) under the leader Pericles.
The Peloponnesian War (431-404 BCE) ended in Athens's defeat. A plague in Athens killed Pericles. The historian Thucydides wrote the war's history.

cards.h: Did 300 Spartans stand alone at Thermopylae?
cards.b:
Myth: only 300 Spartans fought Persia.Fact: they were joined by several thousand other Greeks, including about 700 from Thespiae. Herodotus gives numbers around 7,000.

Also, a favourite tale says Spartans threw weak babies off a cliff. The source is Plutarch, writing centuries later. A 2007 study of the supposed site found only adult remains.

Republics of the Ganges

While Athens tried democracy in 508 BCE, the Ganga plain had its own experiments. Among the 16 mahajanapadas, some were ganas or sanghas, ruled by assemblies of clan heads rather than kings.

The Vajji confederacy, led by the Licchavis of Vaishali, met often in a hall, and the Shakyas and Mallas had similar councils. Votes were counted with coloured sticks. The Buddha praised the Vajjis for meeting regularly, and he borrowed assembly rules for his monastic Sangha.

These republics fell to monarchy. Magadha's Ajatashatru crushed Vaishali, and by the Mauryas the experiment was over.

Five things to remember

  1. Cleisthenes created Athenian democracy around 508 BCE.
  2. Only male citizens voted.
  3. Sparta used helots and trained boys in the agoge.
  4. The Peloponnesian War (431-404 BCE) ended with Sparta's win.
  5. India had gana-sanghas at the same time.

Think about it

  • Can a democracy rest on slavery?
  • Which is more admirable: Athens's openness or Sparta's discipline?
